headline: Pampanga Under Red Rainfall Warning as Habagat Flood Risk Intensifies
seoTitle: Pampanga Under Red Rainfall Warning as Habagat Intensifies | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA placed Pampanga under a Red Rainfall Warning late August 28 as the Southwest Monsoon drove serious flood risk across Central Luzon.
deck: Late-Friday PAGASA warnings placed Pampanga, Zambales and Bataan under Red rainfall conditions as the Southwest Monsoon continued to threaten flood-prone communities.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Pampanga was placed under a Red Rainfall Warning late Friday, August 28, as the Southwest Monsoon continued to dump heavy rain across Central Luzon.

PAGASA's late-evening heavy-rainfall warnings also placed Zambales and Bataan under Red warning conditions, indicating serious flooding risk in flood-prone areas. Parts of Bulacan and Tarlac were likewise covered by Red warnings in the 11:00 PM bulletin.

sections.heading: Flood impacts
paragraphs: The approved FMB News briefing, citing Pampanga disaster authorities and local reporting, said more than 50 barangays had experienced flooding and reported riverbank erosion and structural damage in Lubao. Those local impact figures remain attributed to the briefing pending a consolidated provincial incident report.
Residents in low-lying areas were advised to follow local evacuation instructions and avoid flooded roads, riverbanks and other fast-rising waterways.

sections.heading: Classes and public activity
paragraphs: Several local governments announced Saturday class suspensions as the monsoon continued. Separate current reporting confirmed localized August 29 suspensions in Metro Manila, Bulacan and Pangasinan, while local executives retained authority to issue additional suspensions based on conditions.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Earlier on Friday, Malacañang suspended government work and classes from 1:00 PM in Metro Manila and 16 provinces, including Pampanga, Bataan, Bulacan and Zambales, following an NDRRMC recommendation tied to the enhanced Habagat and a low-pressure area inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A Red Rainfall Warning signals serious flooding risk in vulnerable areas. Even where rain temporarily weakens, runoff can continue to raise rivers and inundate roads after prolonged monsoon rainfall.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should monitor PAGASA's succeeding heavy-rainfall warnings and local disaster advisories because warning levels and affected municipalities can change within hours.
